clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 6258-D is the approval, in the President's words 'pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do adopt and approve the report, recommendations and findings of the Administrator and do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and it is hereby approved'. The order acts under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act and recites the Administrator's findings under section 3(a) of that Act (the held text records the findings on clauses (1) and (2) of subsection (a) of section 3), so the command is a section 3 approval whose operative effect depended on the code-approval provisions of Title I. No earlier end applies: the order states no period, condition or provisional approval, and no held record shows the code cancelled or suspended before June 14, 1935 (see earlier_end_check). The approval ended on June 14, 1935, when Congress approved S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375); its section 2 provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed'. The resolution states no effective date other than its approval and nothing defers section 2, so June 14, 1935 is the end of the prospective operative effect of the approval. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date; June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Actor: Congress, by S.J. Res. 113 section 2.

research_rationale:
EO 6258-D (signed August 26, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Men's Clothing Industry under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, on the application and the Administrator's report, with no other command. Identity: the census register row, the WPA 1944 numbered list entry at p. 537 (August 26, 1933) and the held text agree on number, date and subject. Source: the American Presidency Project transcription (a Common Crawl capture, grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false); the page record with the same sha256 in the mirror documents names this order's number, its date and subject agree with the text, and its text_sha256 is the held text's. The claim follows the reviewed shared analysis of NIRA code approvals (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md, adjudicated 2026-10-29): first end June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 section 2); Schechter recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date; accrued effects survive as past effects.

savings.reason: Nothing continues the approval after the repeal. Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code approved by this order before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, not continued operation of EO 6258-D. The section 5 antitrust exemption for action taken while the code was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for that past action; the resolution's proviso reads 'Provided, That the exemption provided in section 5 of such title shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder', names agreements rather than codes and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle how far it narrowed the exemption for past action under codes. No held source shows a prosecution continued or any action under the code taken after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495, held the code provisions in question invalid on the delegation ground and on the intrastate-commerce ground. It is recorded as a validity characterization of every section 3 code approval (void from issuance under the doctrine prevailing in 1935), not as an end of this order; the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this approval.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of the National Industrial Recovery Act; not an end date
source_notes.reason: Section 3 of Title I states the legal effects of an approved code that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed by description: under 3(b) its provisions are the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry, under 3(c) the district courts may restrain violations, and under 3(f) a violation is a misdemeanor. Cited for the content of the repealed provisions, not for any date.
